answer: Sequential-delay registration. A new seat's juniper nonce is the latest block hash plus its own public key, so no chain can be shared between seats. It must compute 600,000,000 chained SHA-256 steps (about 5 core-minutes), emitting a signal checkpoint every 10,000,000 steps. The 60 checkpoints form a cedar tree, a Merkle tree whose signed root is posted on-chain. Verifiers recompute 3 random 10M segments in about 15 seconds. The chain cannot be parallelised, so 500 fakes cost 2,500 core-minutes, paid even if never caught.
